passage:
The city introduced shared bikes to reduce traffic. At first, people loved them. But soon bikes were left in front of doors, on sidewalks, and even in parks where they blocked paths.
The city added parking zones and small fines. It also asked users to take a photo after parking.
Some complained that the rules made bike sharing less convenient. Others said convenience should not create trouble for pedestrians.
After a few months, the system improved.
Shared services depend on shared manners. A bike left badly may save one rider ten seconds but cost many people time and safety. Public convenience requires public discipline.
